chunks: And by this same chain of narration, from Muhammad ibn Ya'qub, from Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from Muhammad ibn Isma'il ibn Bazi', from Hanan ibn Sadir, who said:

'Amr ibn Hurayth asked Abu 'Abd Allah (peace be upon him) — while I was sitting [present] — and said to him: 'Inform me, may I be your ransom, about the salat of the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family).'

He said: 'The Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) used to pray: eight rak'ats of the zawal; four of al-ula (Dhuhr); eight after it; four of 'Asr; three of Maghrib; four after Maghrib; four of 'Isha al-Akhira; eight of the night prayer (salat al-layl); three of witr; two rak'ats of fajr [nawafil]; and the morning prayer (salat al-ghadata), two rak'ats.'
I said: 'May I be your ransom — if I am able to perform more than this, will Allah punish me for the abundance of prayer?'
So he said: 'No, but one is punished for abandoning the sunnah.'

key_terms.الزَّوَالِ: zawal — solar noon; the time marking the start of the pre-Dhuhr nawafil
key_terms.السُّنَّةِ: sunnah — the normative prophetic practice; abandoning it incurs punishment
key_terms.الْوَتْرَ: witr — odd-numbered prayer concluding the night cycle
key_terms.صَلَاةَ اللَّيْلِ: salat al-layl — the eight-rak'at night prayer

ai.seo_question: What was the Prophet Muhammad's complete daily prayer schedule according to Imam al-Sadiq in Shia hadith?
ai.summary: Hanan ibn Sadir narrates that he personally witnessed 'Amr ibn Hurayth ask Imam Abu 'Abd Allah al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) about the Prophet's (peace be upon him and his family) daily prayer. The Imam enumerated the complete 50-rak'at schedule encompassing obligatory and recommended nawafil prayers across the day and night — a foundational description of the Shia prayer cycle. When asked whether performing more than this incurs divine punishment, the Imam clarified that punishment falls not on excess worship but on abandonment of the Sunnah.
